The ideal candidate is enthusiastic, highly organized, team-oriented, self-motivated, good-humored, and resourceful. The District Staff Assistant will report to the District Director. Responsibilities include overseeing the front office, greeting visitors, answering office phones, processing mail, assisting with constituent casework, drafting correspondence, attending and assisting with outreach events, serving as a constituent service liaison between constituents and the office, and performing other duties as needed. The District Staff Assistant will also be responsible for overseeing a robust internship program, including recruiting, hiring, training, and supervising interns. The District Staff Assistant will also drive the Congresswoman as needed.

description: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter is a physician, a founding member of the Democratic Doctors Caucus, and one of Congress's most committed voices on healthcare, climate, immigrant rights, and working families. Her office is seeking an experienced, creative, and strategic Communications Director in her Washington, D.C. office. This is a senior role with real creative authority. You will set the communications agenda, shape the Congresswoman's public voice, manage a small and talented team, and be a key thought partner to the Chief of Staff, Legislative Director, and District Director. The ability to maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends as necessary—with the ability to flex time during slower periods—is essential. Dexter's Portland-based district is highly engaged, and her communications operation needs to match that energy. This is a fun office that moves fast, takes the work seriously, and believes that good communication is itself a form of advocacy. This is not an entry-level position. Salary starts at $95,000 and is commensurate with experience and qualifications. The office also offers a competitive package of benefits (health insurance, student loan repayment, and more).
responsibilities: Develop and execute a proactive, comprehensive communications strategy across earned media, franked communications, and social platforms.
Draft and review floor speeches, press statements, op-eds, talking points, and social content in the Congresswoman's voice — daily, and often on deadline.
Pitch and field press inquiries across TV, print, radio, and digital media; build and maintain strong relationships with local Oregon and national reporters.

Manage the Congresswoman's franked communications program, including direct mail, digital advertising, mass texts, and monthly telephone town halls, ensuring full compliance with franking regulations.
Oversee the Congresswoman's official website and newsletter program.
Prepare the Congresswoman for press conferences and media appearances; and support field and legislative staff in preparing the Congresswoman for public events in their portfolios.
Collaborate with legislative staff to translate bill introductions, legislative victories, and Floor activity into compelling public narratives.
Proactively work with the District Office to publicize Oregon-based events including town halls and community conversations.
Supervise and mentor a Digital Manager (D.C.) and part-time Press Assistant (Portland).
Respond rapidly to breaking news at the national and district level.

Monitor and engage emerging and new media platforms — including YouTube, Substack, and podcasts — identifying opportunities to expand the Congresswoman's reach and connect with audiences beyond traditional press.
Support video production, graphic design, and photography — our Digital Manager leads on most content creation, but a CD who can backstop in a pinch is essential.
qualifications: This is not an entry-level position; significant prior communications experience is required.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute comprehensive communications strategies across earned media, franked communications, and social platforms.
Strong writing skills with the ability to draft floor speeches, press statements, op-eds, talking points, and social content on deadline.
Experience pitching and fielding press inquiries and building relationships with reporters.
Supervisory experience managing and mentoring communications staff.
Ability to maintain a flexible schedule including evenings and weekends as necessary.
Familiarity with franking regulations and compliance.
Creative and strategic thinker with the ability to serve as a key thought partner to senior leadership.
how_to_apply: Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis. The office will contact the most qualified candidates to begin the interview process in June. To apply, please submit a cover letter and resume to OR03Resumes@mail.house.gov with the subject line: "Communications Director"
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, age, disability, military status, marital or parental status. Women, people of color, and other members of traditionally underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

description: Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-3), a member of the House Ways and Means Committee, is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Legislative Assistant to join the Washington, D.C. office. The portfolio will primarily focus on immigration policy, with the potential to cover health, trade, financial services, or other issues based on office needs and the candidate's expertise. Other priority issues may be added as appropriate. The Legislative Assistant will play a central role in advancing the Congressman's policy agenda. The position involves drafting legislation, preparing policy memoranda, composing letters and talking points, and providing recommendations on legislative votes. The individual in this role will be responsible for monitoring policy developments, analyzing legislative proposals, and offering strategic guidance on how best to advance the Congressman's work. The job requires regular engagement with constituents, advocacy organizations, and stakeholders, as well as close coordination with the legislative, communications, and district office staff. The position requires the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment while maintaining strong attention to detail and meeting tight deadlines.

Ability to build coalitions and recruit both internal and external partners
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Sound judgment

Positive attitude

Comfort working under pressure

description: The Office of Congresswoman LaMonica McIver seeks a dynamic, mission-driven Outreach Manager to strengthen relationships with constituents, community organizations, local leaders, advocacy groups, and stakeholders throughout New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. The Outreach Manager will serve as a key liaison between the Congresswoman and the community, helping ensure residents are informed, engaged, and connected to federal resources and legislative priorities. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator with strong organizational skills, deep community engagement experience, and a passion for public service and constituent advocacy.
responsibilities: Community Engagement: Organizing events, town halls, and meetings to connect with constituents and understand their needs and concerns.
Communication: Managing correspondence with the public, including newsletters, social media updates, and press releases to keep constituents informed about legislative activities and local issues.
Relationship Building: Establishing and maintaining relationships with community organizations, advocacy groups, and local leaders to foster collaboration and support.
Research and Analysis: Gathering and analyzing feedback from constituents to inform the Congressmember's policy positions and legislative priorities.
Advocacy: Representing the Congressmember at community events and meetings to advocate for the member's initiatives and gather insights from the community.
Strategy Development: Developing outreach strategies to increase constituent engagement and participation in the legislative process.
qualifications: A bachelor's degree or higher education level is preferred, including strong academic credentials.
Previous experience is required.
Knowledge of the 10th Congressional District is required as well as a strong understanding of the physical geography of the district.
Ability to converse in Spanish preferred.

Ability to work cooperatively and courteously with others.
Temperament to communicate with a variety of personalities in a tactful, pleasant, and professional manner.
Knowledge of office policies, practices, and procedures.
Knowledge of office computer applications.
Proficiency in word processing.
New Jersey and/or district ties are a plus.

description: Congressman Ro Khanna's district office in Santa Clara has an immediate opening for a Caseworker/Field Representative, which involves both casework and community outreach. This is a non-supervisory position. The starting salary is $71,000 per year. The application process may include several interviews and a practical test of relevant skills. There is one current job vacancy, and the office has the right to fill any number of positions vacant or becoming vacant during the life of postings. This position ends on November 6, 2026 with the option to extend depending on office needs and available budget.
responsibilities: Monitor issues that impact residents, serve as a liaison to federal agencies and state/local representatives, and respond to constituent inquiries through written and oral communication.

Help local residents resolve casework problems with federal government agencies, including US Citizenship & Immigration Services, Department of State, Veterans Affairs, Internal Revenue Service, and Social Security Administration.

Manage active casework, update constituents to ensure that their concerns are handled in a responsive manner, and maintain up-to-date information about all cases and substantive federal procedures and policies that impact casework.

Represent the Congressman in a variety of community activities, including interacting with leaders of community groups and local organizations, as well as local and state elected officials and stakeholders.
Coordinate special projects and help the staff team manage monthly town hall meetings and special events hosted by the Congressman, such as issues-based forums and roundtable meetings.
Work both in the office and perform activities out in the community.
Help train and mentor student interns.
qualifications: A bachelor's degree with strong academic credentials, or equivalent experience/training in legislation or public service (e.g., casework, constituent service, community outreach).
Ability to work cooperatively and courteously with others (both co-workers and constituents). Past customer service experience is strongly preferred.
Strong oral and written communication skills, as well as public speaking experience.
Professional telephone manner and temperament to communicate with a variety of personalities in a tactful, pleasant, and professional manner.
Knowledge of local, state, and federal agencies and departments; and awareness of issues and events in the district in which the Congressman is involved.
Thoroughness, organizational skills, and careful attention to detail.
Ability to exercise discretion and independent judgment in fulfillment of casework responsibilities.
Knowledge of office policies, practices, and procedures; office computer applications; and proficiency in word processing.
Must have a driver's license, access to a car and the ability to drive to perform field work.
Residency in the district is preferred, as is a knowledge of the region.
how_to_apply: Please e-mail a cover letter, brief writing sample and resume to District Director Tom Pyke (tom.pyke@mail.house.gov) and Director of Constituent Services Simeone Chien (simeone.chien@mail.house.gov). Phone (408) 436-2720. All successful candidates must meet citizenship-related requirements and undergo a security check.
